name: herdr
why: I'm currently using herde[1] to handle/supervise multiple agents

quotes.excerpt: I use herdr a lot If anything, with things like libghostty, I expect more desktop apps with built in terminals. Instead of me having to go to the browser for github, jira, etc, have it all in one app along with whatever terminal tooling you're using Or more likely, based on what the other engineers I work with are doing, we will all vibecode our own tooling that fit our individual workflow
quotes.story: Ask HN: Why are there not more terminal apps?

quotes.excerpt: I'm currently using herde[1] to handle/supervise multiple agents (with some patches I need to try to upstream) along with Nono[2] for sandboxing. This sandboxing approach avoids use of a microVM, which lets me use tooling I already have installed inside the sandbox. The downside is getting all the policies correct as it seems every project needs some new type of access, though Nono does try to make policy writing eas
